content:
Hi, I am researching formatter for lean 4. There are a couple of github repos. But it seems to me none of them implemented the recommended style guide (https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/master/doc/std/style.md).

https://github.com/codygunton/lean-fmt, https://github.com/toku-sa-n/leanfmt). Are there 'official' supported formatter that implements the recommended style guide?
There's also an unofficial Lean fork by wvhulle with a formatter which is what I've been using for the past few months.

I couldn't wait and made one myself (https://github.com/duckki/LeanFmt), partly because my preference is slightly different from Lean community guidance.

I want operators to lead wrapped-around lines like this:

def parenthesizedConjunctionChain (schema : Schema) : Prop :=
  namesAreUnique (schema.allTypes.map TypeDefinition.name)
  ∧ schema.objectType schema.queryType
  ∧ (∀ typeDefinition,
      typeDefinition ∈ schema.types -> typeDefinitionWellFormed schema typeDefinition)
  ∧ (∀ typeName objectTypeName,
      objectTypeName ∈ schema.getPossibleTypes typeName
      -> schema.objectType objectTypeName)

It works well on my project (https://github.com/duckki/GraphQL.lean).
I'm currently going though mathlib for robustness. I think I can finish it in about a week.

Since then, I've improved the formatter and validated it over mathlib and hex-dev.

  • It uses Lean's own parser and environment for syntax extensions.
  • It preserves code tokens and comments, and is conservative: when its preservation, parsing, or idempotency checks do not pass, it leaves the original source intact.

You can add it in your lakefile:

[[require]]
name = "leanfmt"
git = "https://github.com/duckki/leanfmt.git"
rev = "v0.3.5"

Then run lake update --keep-toolchain, and for example:

lake exe fmt --check -r MyProject

I’ve written more about the design, safety model, and validation—including a complete Mathlib formatting/build validation—in the announcement post. Feedback, bug reports, and examples of layouts that need improvement are very welcome.
